rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord is prohibited from terminating a tenancy without just cause. Just cause consists solely of at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy as defined in Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(b); document-wide]; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction with a government agency, or other document for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, but this exemption does not include Section 8 voucher housing. [§ 98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the California Mobilehome Residency Law are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(g); document-wide]; Rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence at the property is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(h); document-wide]; Single-family residences occupied by the landlord as their principal residence where the landlord rents no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two junior ADUs, or a mobilehome, are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(i); document-wide]; Two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupied one unit as their principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt from this Division, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [§ 98.0703(k); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required statutory exemption notice is provided to the tenant in the lease. [§ 98.0703(l); document-wide]
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.requirement: If a court or government agency determines that the tenant is at fault for the condition triggering the order or need to vacate, the tenant is not entitled to relocation assistance under section 98.0706(c).

rules.key_value: not less than three times the required relocation assistance
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy as defined in Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(b); document-wide]; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction with a government agency, or other document for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, but this exemption does not include Section 8 voucher housing. [§ 98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the California Mobilehome Residency Law are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(g); document-wide]; Rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence at the property is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(h); document-wide]; Single-family residences occupied by the landlord as their principal residence where the landlord rents no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two junior ADUs, or a mobilehome, are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(i); document-wide]; Two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupied one unit as their principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt from this Division, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [§ 98.0703(k); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required statutory exemption notice is provided to the tenant in the lease. [§ 98.0703(l); document-wide]

rule.title: Notice and Opportunity to Cure for Curable Lease Violations
rule.requirement: Before terminating for a curable lease violation, the landlord must provide written notice describing the violation and giving an opportunity to cure. If uncured within the notice period, the landlord may serve a three-day notice to quit.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to at-fault just cause terminations that are curable lease violations.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy as defined in Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(b); document-wide]; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction with a government agency, or other document for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, but this exemption does not include Section 8 voucher housing. [§ 98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the California Mobilehome Residency Law are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(g); document-wide]; Rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence at the property is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(h); document-wide]; Single-family residences occupied by the landlord as their principal residence where the landlord rents no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two junior ADUs, or a mobilehome, are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(i); document-wide]; Two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupied one unit as their principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt from this Division, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [§ 98.0703(k); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required statutory exemption notice is provided to the tenant in the lease. [§ 98.0703(l); document-wide]

scope_inputs.coverage_conditions: Applies if the property is offered for rent within five years of an eviction under § 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4).

citation.model_span:
If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential 
purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under 
sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the 
residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by 
the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:   
(1) advised the landlord in writing within 30 days of the termination 
notice of the tenant’s desire to receive an offer to renew the tenancy; 
and  
(2) provided the landlord a mailing address or email address for the 
landlord to send the offer, including any change of mailing address or 
email address.  
The landlord shall have the right to screen the tenant using industry accepted 
methods and shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written 
offer for the new tenancy. The tenant shall have 30 days from the date of 
receipt of the offer to accept.

rule.requirement: A breach of a material term of the lease as described in California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), including violation of a lease provision after being issued written notice to correct, constitutes an enumerated at-fault just cause ground for termination of tenancy.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy as defined in Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(b); document-wide]; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction with a government agency, or other document for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, but this exemption does not include Section 8 voucher housing. [§ 98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the California Mobilehome Residency Law are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(g); document-wide]; Rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence at the property is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(h); document-wide]; Single-family residences occupied by the landlord as their principal residence where the landlord rents no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two junior ADUs, or a mobilehome, are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(i); document-wide]; Two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupied one unit as their principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt from this Division, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [§ 98.0703(k); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required statutory exemption notice is provided to the tenant in the lease. [§ 98.0703(l); document-wide]

rule.title: At-Fault Just Cause: Use for Unlawful Purpose
rule.requirement: The tenant's use of the residential rental property for an unlawful purpose as described in California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(4) constitutes an enumerated at-fault just cause ground for termination of tenancy.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy as defined in Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(b); document-wide]; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction with a government agency, or other document for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, but this exemption does not include Section 8 voucher housing. [§ 98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the California Mobilehome Residency Law are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(g); document-wide]; Rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence at the property is exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(h); document-wide]; Single-family residences occupied by the landlord as their principal residence where the landlord rents no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two junior ADUs, or a mobilehome, are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(i); document-wide]; Two-unit properties in a single structure where the landlord occupied one unit as their principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy are exempt from this Division. [§ 98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt from this Division, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [§ 98.0703(k); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required statutory exemption notice is provided to the tenant in the lease. [§ 98.0703(l); document-wide]

evidence_parts.quoted_text:
(l) residential rental property, including a mobilehome, that is alienable separate 
from the title to any other dwelling unit, provided that both of the following 
apply: 
(1) The landlord is not any of the following: 
(A) a real estate investment trust, as defined in California Internal 
Revenue Code section 856, as may be amended;

(B) a corporation; 
(C) a limited liability company in which at least one member is a 
corporation; or  
 
(D) management of a mobilehome park, as defined in California 
Civil Code section 798.2, as may be amended. 
(2) The tenants have been provided written notice that the residential 
rental property is exempt from this Division using the following 
statement:

Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal 
Code. This property meets the requirements of San Diego 
Municipal Code section 98.0703(l) and the landlord is not any 
of the following: (1) a real estate investment trust, as defined 
by California Internal Revenue Code section 856; (2) a 
corporation; (3) a limited liability company in which at least 
one member is a corporation; or (4) management of a 
mobilehome park, as defined in California Civil Code 
section 798.2.  
 
For a tenancy existing before January 1, 2024, the notice required 
above may be provided in the lease. For a tenancy commenced or 
renewed on or after January 1, 2024, the notice required above shall be 
provided in the lease.

provisions.summary: Prohibition on terminating a tenancy without just cause.
Enumerated grounds for at-fault just cause eviction.
No-fault just cause ground for owner or relative occupancy and related conditions.
No-fault just cause ground for withdrawal from the rental market.
No-fault just cause ground for government order, court order, or local ordinance to vacate.
No-fault just cause ground for demolition or substantial remodel.
Mandatory written notice to tenants regarding rent caps and just cause protections.
Requirement to provide the Tenant Protection Guide.
Timing for notice and guide provision for pre-existing tenancies.
Requirement to include notice and guide in lease or signed writing for new or renewed tenancies.
Requirement to give written notice and opportunity to cure before at-fault termination for curable breach.
Requirement to notify the Housing Commission within three business days of an at-fault termination notice.
Notice requirements for no-fault termination of tenancy.
Requirement to notify the Housing Commission within three business days of a no-fault termination notice.
Requirement to provide relocation assistance (2 months or 3 months for seniors/disabled) by payment or rent waiver.
Single direct payment allowed for relocation assistance to multiple tenants.
Relocation assistance is in addition to the return of any deposit or security amounts.
Credit of relocation assistance against other relocation assistance required by law.
Landlord recovery of relocation assistance as damages if tenant fails to vacate.
Displaced tenant right of first return / offer to renew within five years of no-fault eviction.
Failure to strictly comply with § 98.0706 renders any termination notice void.
Injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money/punitive damages for violations.
Affirmative defense in an action to recover possession based on violation of Division.
Wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times actual economic damages.
Liability for not less than three times required relocation assistance and actual economic damages.
Discretionary attorney's fees and costs for material violation in attempting to recover possession.
Failure to comply with any provision of Division renders any notice of termination void.
